newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot busy, vols rise.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot busy, vols rise.

text.p: Options on shares of Office Depot Inc drew heavy interest Tuesday as the office superstore's proposed merger with Staples Inc was being debated in Washington, traders said.
On Monday, the U.S. government opened its case against the proposed $4 billion merger, arguing that a combined company could raise prices on a wide range of office products.

The five-day hearing will give both sides the chance to call witnesses and present evidence before Judge Thomas Hogan, who is scheduled to rule in June whether to grant the Federal Trade Commission a preliminary injunction against the merger.
Traders said with most of the Office Depot options activity in the July series, the investors appeared to be playing for a decision after the June expiration on June 21.
Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said institutional investors were doing various put spreads.
The July 15 puts were the most active Office Depot put, with turnover of about 5,350 contracts by early afternoon. The July 17-1/2 put traded about 3,825 and the July 12-1/2 puts traded about 2,615.
"There's also been demand for July 17 calls and July 20 calls," Schwarz said.
The July 20 calls traded 6,705 contracts, the July 17-1/2 calls traded 4,225 and the July 15 calls traded 1,400.
"As a result of this we've seen volatility run from a very high 85 to well over 100," Schwarz added.
Volatilities in the Office Depot June options were in the 80 to 90 zone.
Office Depot shares were unchanged at 16-1/4. More than 1.2 million shares changed hands.
The most active Office Depot June option was the 17-1/2 call, with turnover of 1,785 contracts. The June 15 call traded about 750 and the June 15 put traded 335.
"Most of the June activity is hedging off some July risk," one trader said.
But even if the judge grants the FTC a preliminary injunction against the Office Depot-Staples merger, the next step would be a months-long trial before an FTC administrative law judge.
The five-member FTC has already voted twice to halt the merger.
Staples options, which trade on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, were quiet, with the July 22-1/2 and September 30 calls each trading 500 contracts.
The Staples June 20 and July 20 put each traded roughly 150 contracts and the July 22-1/2 put traded 100.
